summary: Gov. Maura Healey (Democrat) ran for re-election and won over Mike Minogue (Republican).

candidates.name: Maura Healey
candidates.bio: Maura Healey is a Democrat who was first elected governor of Massachusetts in 2022. She ran with Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll.

positions.summary: Says her administration cut taxes for the first time in more than 20 years and is building 100,000 new homes.
Says she was the first governor to cap health care deductibles and co-pays.
Says her administration doubled school funding, made school meals free, and made community college free for everyone.
Says she opposed utility rate increases and launched an Energy Affordability Agenda to take $13 billion off energy bills.
Says protecting reproductive freedom is among her accomplishments.

candidates.name: Mike Minogue
candidates.bio: Mike Minogue is a Republican, an Army veteran and a political newcomer who led the medical device company Abiomed for close to two decades. He won the Republican primary for governor on September 1, 2026, defeating Brian Shortsleeve.

positions.summary: Says his plan centers on accountability, affordability including lower taxes, and public safety.
Says he would use third-party healthcare auditors to find waste, fraud and abuse.
Says he would end sanctuary state policies and prioritize removing violent criminals and drug dealers.
Says he would cancel the state's 2050 net-zero emissions mandate and focus on energy innovation to lower costs.
Says he is not personally pro-abortion but would support Massachusetts' abortion law and FDA approval of abortion medications.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called). 2026-11-25: not marked certified. Shares are from the Secretary of the Commonwealth's election statistics site, with blanks left out. A local news report (https://franklinobserver.town.news/g/franklin-town-ma/n/398885/galvin-crunches-numbers-near-record-mid-term-turnout) says city and town officials certified results Nov 18, but no Secretary of the Commonwealth page was opened that says the 2026 general election results are certified.
